The level of the tender committee to consider final price offers is determined on the basis of the lowest initial price offer of the qualified bid. A tender is a formal offer to supply/execute at quoted rates; railways invite open tenders to ensure competition and transparency. Remember: Eliminate the distractors first — each wrong option usually describes a related but different concept.

q: The level of Tender Committee to consider Final Price Offers shall be determined on the basis of lowest initial price offer of bid qualfied for award of contract in case of works and service Tenders, and qualified bulk order in case of Stores Tenders as opened:

options.B: Prior to Reverse Auction, on the basis of highest initial price offer
options.C: Prior to Reverse Auction, on the basis of lowest initial price offer, with approval of GM
options.D: After Reverse Auction, on the basis of final price offers

e: Option C (offer) is the correct choice. option (C): the level of the Tender Committee to consider the final price offers is fixed *prior to* the reverse auction, with the GM's approval, on the basis of the initial price offer as opened — not on the post-auction final price. Railway Board's reverse-auction instructions require this determination before RA starts, using the lowest initial price offer of the bid qualified for award (works/services) or the qualified bulk order (stores) as opened. This prevents the TC level from shifting after prices fall in the auction.

q: AIl bidders eligible for benefits under Public Procurement Order -2017(Make in India) found qualified for Bulk order/Award of Contract and are within the specified range of Price preference to participate in the Reverse Auction irrespective of their inter-se ranking:

options.B: Shall not be allowed
options.C: Shall be allowed with the approval of PCMM

e: Correct option (A): such bidders *shall be permitted* to join the reverse auction. Approach by elimination: strike out the options that contradict the basic principle, and the survivor is your answer. Building this elimination habit speeds up the paper considerably. Remember: Link this to the connected chapter topic; cross-topic twists are common in this exam. Watch the timeline or sequence in such questions; many errors come from mixing up the order.

q: In the case of Tenders for procurement of Goods and Services (Other than Consultancy)under e-RA, where the L1 offer withdraws his bid the Tender subject to conditions_

options.B: Need not be discharged
options.C: Need to be discharged with the approval of PCMM

e: Option B (Need not be discharged) is the correct choice. option (B): the tender *need not be discharged*. Per Railway Board instructions on e-RA for goods and services, if the L1 offerer withdraws his bid during the reverse auction, the tender is not required to be discharged; the Tender Committee can consider the next eligible bidder for award, subject to the applicable conditions. Discharge is therefore not mandatory merely because L1 walked away.

q: All Tenders of 'Earnings Contracts' in IR shall be done through

options.B: IREPS mode

e: Option B (IREPS mode) is the correct choice. option (B): all earnings contracts on Indian Railways are done through *IREPS mode*. Earnings contracts are revenue-earning contracts (catering, advertisements, parking, stalls, etc.) handled through the Indian Railways E-Procurement System, the Railways' mandated electronic tendering platform. Manual-only or other electronic modes are not permitted for these contracts.

q: The Letter of Credit operating charges collected from the parties in Stores Contracts are credited t0

options.B: Stock Adjustment Account Earnings

e: Correct option (C): the letter-of-credit operating charges collected from the parties in stores contracts are credited to the suspense-type head shown at option (C), and not to final heads of account, the stock adjustment account, or the stores-in-stock accoun. Approach by elimination: strike out the options that contradict the basic principle, and the survivor is your answer. Building this elimination habit speeds up the paper considerably.

q: The cardinal points which differentiate material checking from Stock Verification and to be borne in mind by the Stock verification staff are

options.A: Physical Verification of the Stores; Review of Maxima/Minima with reference to the AAC
options.B: Analysis of overstock/surplus stores and review action taken thereon
options.C: Analysis of special aspects like storage conditions, proneness to pilferage, deterioration/ obsolescence and other aspects of Inventory management, Test check to verify the correctness of information furnished in indents/requisitions for revision of imprest schedules to ensure that no over indenting of stores is resorted to by the custodians

e: All of the above — that is the right answer. option (D): all the listed points are the cardinal differences. Stock verification by accounts staff is far wider than mere material checking (physical counting): it includes reviewing maxima/minima against the AAC, analysing overstocked/surplus stores and the action taken, examining storage conditions, proneness to pilferage, deterioration and obsolescence, and test-checking indents/requisitions and imprest schedules to ensure custodians are not over-indenting.

q: To do Justice to the enormous responsibility; ISAs and ASVs are expected to be more resourceful with clear knowledge about stores and their accountal including various financial implications: i)Ordinarily the duties of ISAs are supervisory in nature over functioning of ASVs. ii)In case of exigencies, all assigned duties of the Stock verifiers may also be entrusted to the ISAs to bring in effectiveness and quality in Stock verification:

options.B: Statement ii) is only correct
options.C: Statements i) and ii) are correct
options.D: Statement i) and ii) are not correct

e: Correct option (C): both statements are correct. The key is the precise meaning the question tests: each option describes a closely related but distinct idea, and only one fits the definition exactly. In the exam, such questions reward careful reading of definitions — compare every option against the textbook meaning word by word. Remember: Remember the underlying principle, not just the sentence: examiners often rephrase the same concept.

q: Sr.ISA of Stores Accounts Office is responsible for maintenance of manual Manuscript Register (S.3206) separately for each Depot and Line verification

options.A: One Register for each Financial year
options.B: One Register for his tenure of posting attached to the depotldepots

e: The correct answer is (A) only Correct. option (C): only statement (A) is correct. The Sr. ISA of the Stores Accounts Office maintains the manual Manuscript Register (S.3206) separately for each depot and for line verification — one register for each financial year. It is not maintained as a single register covering his whole tenure of posting at the depot(s), so statement (B) is wrong. A useful way to verify this in the exam hall is to ask what would break if the opposite were true — the logic of the underlying system points straight to this option.

q: In addition to his normal duties Sr.ISA is responsible for

options.A: Prepare programme of work for each financial year at stores depots/online well before commencement of financial year; obtain approval of FA&CAO
options.B: Distribute the programme chalked out for the financial year in such a way that the programme will be completed as per Schedule.
options.C: Train the ASVs in various branches of work stock verification and guide them continuously and constantly for qualitative work:

e: The correct answer is All of the above. option (D): all of the above. In addition to normal duties, the Sr. ISA prepares the programme of work for each financial year at stores depots and on line well before the year begins and obtains the FA&CAO's approval, distributes the chalked-out programme so it is completed as per schedule, and trains the ASVs in the various branches of stock-verification work, guiding them continuously for qualitative output.

q: A field Book Register (S.3213) having particulars of details of 'Field Books Issued to ASVs' duly allotting the Number and office stamp etc , is maintained by:_

options.B: Depot Officer

e: The correct answer is SrISA. option (A): the Field Book Register (S.3213) — recording the particulars and allotted numbers of field books issued to ASVs, duly stamped with the office stamp — is maintained by the Sr. ISA. It is the Sr. ISA's control register over the field books (the Register of Verification) used by the stock verifiers under him. A useful way to verify this in the exam hall is to ask what would break if the opposite were true — the logic of the underlying system points straight to this option.

q: A surprise check of stock of diesellpetrol including overhauling of Accounts at RCDs(Rail Consumer Depots) is to be done by

options.B: Stores Accounts Officer

e: The correct answer is SrISA. option (C): the surprise check of diesel/petrol stocks, including overhauling of the accounts, at Rail Consumer Depots (RCDs) is done by the Sr. ISA. Fuel stocks are high-value and pilferage-prone, so this surprise check is entrusted to the senior inspecting officer of the stores accounts organisation rather than to the ASV or the depot officer. A useful way to verify this in the exam hall is to ask what would break if the opposite were true — the logic of the underlying system points straight to this option.
